A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLM3D work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 ends with references; v2 includes Appendices A–D. The supplied material supports reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM3D results on 110 GPTEval3D prompts, feed-forward generation results in Table 2, and qualitative sensitivity and ablation experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds quantitative ablations, runtime and memory measurements, external 3D-native evaluations, and additional generated examples.

M1.justification: The dual-criterion Yes/No log-odds critic, SDS objective, annealing strategy and test-time gradient guidance remain unchanged in Sections 4.1–4.3. Appendix A newly documents differentiable preprocessing, reference-image conditioning and implementation algorithms; it does not establish a revision to the existing method.

E1.justification: The 110-prompt GPTEval3D benchmark and existing text- and image-conditioned 3D generation settings remain. Additional household-object and scene examples in Appendix D stay within this coverage; no new dataset or distinct task scenario is identified.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes Fantasia3D, Instant3D and Magic3D from the reported comparison. The other seven baselines, including DreamReward and DreamDPO, remain, and Table 2 retains CLAY and Hunyuan3D. This narrows the comparison without replacing its principal competitors.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds substantial evaluation designs: point-cloud ULIP/Uni3D text and image alignment, gradient/reward measurements at three optimization checkpoints, four guidance schedules, and SDS-only/VLM-only/combined comparisons using CLIP cosine similarity. Existing Elo and 50-step sampling protocols remain. Table 2 newly specifies 24 prompts, but the PDFs do not establish an increase in sample count.

E4.justification: v2 adds prompt-formulation comparisons, content-only versus geometry-only diagnostics, guidance-schedule ablations, VLM-only optimization controls, and computational profiling in Appendices B–C. These investigate critic complementarity, guidance timing, the contribution of SDS and computational cost. The original geometry-query/multiview ablation is retained as Figure 7, previously Figure 6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, dispersion estimates or significance tests. The new appendix tables continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty analysis.

E6.justification: Shared entries in Tables 1–2 are numerically unchanged, while three Table 1 rows disappear. Tables 3–7 add substantive findings, including CLIP scores of 0.290 for SDS-only, 0.271 for VLM-only and 0.317 for combined VLM3D, alongside new ULIP/Uni3D results and visual examples. Table 3 reports 120 seconds for guided feed-forward generation, conflicting with the retained 60-second statement in Section 5.2.

T1.justification: Appendix C newly defines the paper-specific Geometry Score as the equal-weight average of Chamfer, Hausdorff and symmetric point-to-mesh distances between normalized meshes. This is a limited mathematical-definition addition. The core diffusion and critic equations remain unchanged, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contribution: a differentiable semantic and spatial VLM critic applicable to both optimization-based and native 3D generation. Claims about semantic alignment, geometric consistency and cross-paradigm novelty retain their scope.

C2.justification: Appendices B–C add interpretations concerning specific geometric checklists, complementary semantic/geometric signals and meaningful VLM-only optimization gradients. They also identify VLM memory consumption as a bottleneck and suggest smaller backbones or quantization. These refine the existing account; the main interpretations and limitations concerning long, detailed prompts remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A supplies two algorithms, Torch-based differentiable preprocessing, the reference-image/rasterization pipeline, and concrete settings such as 10,000–15,000 updates, learning rate 0.001, guidance decay from 10 to 0 and 512×512 rendering. It also documents baseline provenance and code/attachment access statements. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing that the underlying experiments changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for PaliGemma, RLHF, ULIP and Uni3D, and explicitly relates its reward optimization to RLHF. The Fantasia3D reference is removed. The main related-work organization and research positioning remain substantially unchanged; the switch to author–year citations is stylistic.

P1.justification: The original section sequence and most main-text prose remain closely matched. v2 makes limited wording and author-affiliation edits, adds impact and acknowledgment sections, and organizes supplementary material into Appendices A–D. The expansion primarily supplies technical content rather than extensively rewriting the original argument.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3–7, a prompt-comparison Figure 6, four multiview galleries in Figures 8–11, algorithm blocks and boxed prompts. The original Figure 6 moves to the appendix as Figure 7 with its visual content retained. Conference formatting also changes headers, typography and page layout, while Table 1 has fewer rows.

improvement.justification: The appendices substantially address v1's sparse implementation documentation and limited quantitative examination of design choices. Concrete algorithms and settings improve reproducibility, while query/schedule/VLM-only ablations and independent 3D-native metrics strengthen assessment of the critic. These gains outweigh the narrower Table 1 comparison. The improvement remains qualified by the unresolved 60-versus-120-second runtime inconsistency and continued lack of uncertainty reporting.
